messages:
Alex: hey team, quick onboarding question — I have a sandbox token from the welcome email but need to demo a streaming chat from our CI. Is it acceptable to use the sandbox there or should I request a hosted key? Also our security group needs egress IPs to allowlist. Any guidance?

OnboardBot: welcome! :wave: sandbox tokens are meant for interactive use and expire. For CI demos a hosted dev key is better. You can request one via Console -> Settings -> API Keys or ask your manager to approve a dev key.

Diego: +1 hosted for CI. For demo runs we issue a hosted key scoped to the repo with lowered quotas (10 req/s, 40k tokens/day) so it doesn't spike billing. If you only need a single short demo you can run locally with sandbox and refresh the token.

Alex: thanks — how about streaming limits specifically? will streaming cause immediate throttles?

Diego: streaming consumes tokens as the model emits them. If you stream long outputs concurrently you can hit token/day limits first, or per-second request limits. If you see 429s look for Retry-After in the response, back off, and we can provide a temporary uplift for demos.

Priya: security note: never commit keys. Use Vault path secret/onboarding/<your-username> for sandbox and secret/teams/<team>/redwood for hosted. For allowlist requests, infra prefers DNS allow (api.redwood.example.com) but we also publish CIDRs in the internal networking doc — those CIDRs can change. If you need stable IPs for demos, ask for a dedicated NAT or consider Dedicated/Private deployments.

Alex: awesome, I'll grab a hosted dev key from my manager and ping if we need a temporary uplift. Appreciate it! :thumbsup:
